citation.title: Learning hyperparameter predictors for similarity-based multidisciplinary topology optimization
citation.authors: Mariusz Bujny, Muhammad Salman Yousaf, Nathan Zurbrugg, Duane Detwiler, Stefan Menzel, Satchit Ramnath, Thiago Rios, Fabian Duddeck

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: A learned hyperparameter predictor replaces repeated similarity-based TO sampling with prediction from one standard TO run, reducing the computational work needed to choose a target similarity level.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Results report that the approach has 12 times lower computation time than the previous approach at the sampling resolution used (Results, Fig. 8 discussion).
claim.alternatives: Abstract also reports generalization from a linear-elastic training problem to nonlinear crash and industrial car-hood optimization.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP with Energy Scaling Method; repeated TO runs across energy-scaling hyperparameters
baseline.implementation: SIMP and Hybrid Cellular Automata (HCA) implementations described in Methods/results
baseline.problem_size: Training benchmark uses 100×100 elements; car hood is 3D industrial-scale (Methods; Figs. 4, 13)
baseline.classical_time: Previous repeated-sampling approach reported as 12× higher computation time for the experimental sampling resolution (Results, Fig. 8 discussion)
baseline.data_generation_cost: 600 case-reference pairs; 7,800 TO runs generate 7,200 training samples (Methods, training data generation)
baseline.quality_metric: Similarity dissimilarity metric s; crash and car-hood results use TO performance criteria (Results)
baseline.quality_gap: Model test-set R²=0.96 and RMSE=0.027 for predicted s(p) curves (Results).

R1.evidence: Abstract and Conclusion: lower computation cost is claimed for predicting similarity levels without an equal-quality, matched-time or matched-evaluation comparison.

R2.evidence: Methods and Results: no R2 criterion establishing a weak classical solver or hardware mismatch.

R3.evidence: Methods reports 7,800 TO runs used to generate 7,200 samples, but training/data costs are not fully timed and no break-even is reported.

R4.evidence: Results report similarity-based TO outputs and their performance, but do not report infeasible or failed design rates.

reporting.n_test_cases: 60 held-out test pairs from 600 pairs; further nonlinear 2D crash and 3D car-hood demonstrations (Results; Methods).

notes: Data and simulation models are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request; ESM source code is publicly linked, but public runnable code for the full benchmark was not established.
